Patients: Four patients with GI-aGVHD (steroid-resistant, n=3; steroid-dependent, n=1)
Results: FMT was safely performed in patients, with three complete and one partial responses.
Four of the 10 patients treated with FMT had sustained remission of GI-GvHD.
After receiving the FMTs, the clinical symptoms of all patients were relieved, bacteria were enriched, and microbiota compositions were reconstructed.

Patients: 41 patients with steroid-refractory GI-GVHD (FMT, n=23; placebo, n=18)
Results: Clinical remission was significantly greater in the FMT group than in the control group. The FMT group showed a better overall survival (OS). The median survival time was >539 days in the FMT group and 107 days in the control group.

Patients: 26 patients with aGVHD (FMT, n=18; placebo, n=8)
Results: FMT may have protective effects against aGVHD, especially in patients with more severe microbiota disruptions.
In the first patient, FMT resulted in the complete resolution of symptoms. FMT eliminated drug-resistant pathogens, namely very drug-resistant Enterococcus spp.
The overall response rate (ORR) in cases of aGVHD reached 57%, including complete response (CR) in 42% of procedures.
